title: Adani Energy Solutions wins 25-year deal to supply 1,750 MW of round-the-clock green power to Bengal
dek: The state power distributor's award could rise to 2,500 MW. Supply is due to start in July 2028.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Adani Energy Solutions said a wholly owned subsidiary, Powerpulse Trading Solutions, has won a letter of award from the West Bengal State Electricity Distribution Company (WBSEDCL) to supply 1,750 MW of round-the-clock renewable power for 25 years, after an e-reverse auction.

The award includes a "greenshoe" option for another 750 MW which, if WBSEDCL exercises it, would take the contract to 2,500 MW, the company said, according to reports. Supply of the first 1,750 MW is due to begin on 1 July 2028, and of the optional 750 MW from 1 April 2029. The tariff has not been disclosed. A letter of award precedes a formal power purchase agreement, which has not yet been reported as signed.

Round-the-clock renewable contracts require the supplier to deliver clean power at all hours, which means combining solar and wind generation with battery storage. Powerpulse has tied up about 4.6 GW of solar and wind capacity and about 3.5 GWh of battery storage for its contracts, according to reports.

"Round-the-clock renewable power will be critical to India's energy transition," said Kandarp Patel, the company's chief executive, adding that the award reflected the company's partnership with WBSEDCL on the state's long-term power needs. WBSEDCL, the state-owned distributor, supplies electricity to most of West Bengal outside the areas served by the private utility CESC in and around Kolkata.
